statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, let n = len(num). A subsequence of num is a strictly increasing sequence of indices p_0 < p_1 < ... < p_{k-1} with 0 <= p_t < n. Its value is the base-10 integer represented by the digits num[p_0], num[p_1], ..., num[p_{k-1}] in that order, with leading zeros allowed; the empty subsequence (k = 0) has value 0. A subsequence is special if its value is divisible by 25. Let L be the maximum length k of a special subsequence of num. Then r = n - L. Equivalently, r is the smallest integer d with 0 <= d <= n for which there exists a subsequence of num of length n - d whose value is divisible by 25.
preconditions: 1 <= len(num) <= 100; for every i with 0 <= i < len(num), 48 <= num[i] <= 57 (i.e., num[i] is an ASCII digit '0' through '9').

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result (it does not fail, overflow, or panic).
preconditions: 1 <= len(num) <= 100; for every i with 0 <= i < len(num), 48 <= num[i] <= 57 (i.e., num[i] is an ASCII digit '0' through '9').

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, 0 <= r <= len(num).
preconditions: 1 <= len(num) <= 100; for every i with 0 <= i < len(num), 48 <= num[i] <= 57 (i.e., num[i] is an ASCII digit '0' through '9').

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if the entire string num represents a decimal integer divisible by 25, then r = 0.
preconditions: 1 <= len(num) <= 100; for every i with 0 <= i < len(num), 48 <= num[i] <= 57 (i.e., num[i] is an ASCII digit '0' through '9').

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if len(num) = 1, then r = 0 when num[0] = '0' and r = 1 when num[0] != '0'.
preconditions: 1 <= len(num) <= 100; for every i with 0 <= i < len(num), 48 <= num[i] <= 57 (i.e., num[i] is an ASCII digit '0' through '9').

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if there exists an index i with 0 <= i < len(num) and num[i] = '0', then r <= len(num) - 1.
preconditions: 1 <= len(num) <= 100; for every i with 0 <= i < len(num), 48 <= num[i] <= 57 (i.e., num[i] is an ASCII digit '0' through '9').

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if there exist indices i < j with (num[i], num[j]) in {('0','0'), ('2','5'), ('5','0'), ('7','5')}, then r <= len(num) - i - 2.
preconditions: 1 <= len(num) <= 100; for every i with 0 <= i < len(num), 48 <= num[i] <= 57 (i.e., num[i] is an ASCII digit '0' through '9').

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if there exists at least one pair of indices i < j with (num[i], num[j]) in {('0','0'), ('2','5'), ('5','0'), ('7','5')}, let i_max be the largest i for which such a j exists. Then r = len(num) - i_max - 2.
preconditions: 1 <= len(num) <= 100; for every i with 0 <= i < len(num), 48 <= num[i] <= 57 (i.e., num[i] is an ASCII digit '0' through '9').

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if there is no pair i < j with (num[i], num[j]) in {('0','0'), ('2','5'), ('5','0'), ('7','5')}, but there exists an index i with num[i] = '0', then r = len(num) - 1.
preconditions: 1 <= len(num) <= 100; for every i with 0 <= i < len(num), 48 <= num[i] <= 57 (i.e., num[i] is an ASCII digit '0' through '9').

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if num contains no '0' and there is no pair i < j with (num[i], num[j]) in {('0','0'), ('2','5'), ('5','0'), ('7','5')}, then r = len(num).
preconditions: 1 <= len(num) <= 100; for every i with 0 <= i < len(num), 48 <= num[i] <= 57 (i.e., num[i] is an ASCII digit '0' through '9').

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, there exists a subsequence of num of length len(num) - r whose decimal value is divisible by 25.
preconditions: 1 <= len(num) <= 100; for every i with 0 <= i < len(num), 48 <= num[i] <= 57 (i.e., num[i] is an ASCII digit '0' through '9').

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every subsequence of num of length strictly greater than len(num) - r, its decimal value is not divisible by 25.
preconditions: 1 <= len(num) <= 100; for every i with 0 <= i < len(num), 48 <= num[i] <= 57 (i.e., num[i] is an ASCII digit '0' through '9').
